content.text:
The pattern matches KRuO4 (mp-14005) alone.

- **KRuO4 fits:** its simulated peaks line up with the observed ones in both position and relative intensity:

  | Simulated (°) | Observed (°) | Relative intensity (sim / obs) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 16.75 | 16.85 | ~39 / 38 |
  | 25.2 | 25.25 | 100 / 100 |
  | 27.1 | 27.15 | ~14 / 15 |
  | 31.5 | 31.5 | ~18 / 22 |
  | ~44.2 | ~44.4 | ~26 / 27 |
  | ~47.5 | ~47.0 | ~8 / 10 |
  | ~50.2 | ~50.3 | ~15 / 15 |
  | ~55.2 | ~55.3 | ~23 / 21 |

  The smaller peaks near 37, 53.5 and 56 also match roughly.
- **Anatase TiO2 (mp-390) is ruled out as a second phase:** it also has its strongest peak near 25.3°, but its other strong peaks are missing. It predicts about 29 at roughly 48°, where the observed pattern shows only a dip between the 47° and 50.3° peaks. It also cannot explain the 16.85° peak.
- **Not checked:** I only simulated these two candidates. The other seven were not compared directly, but KRuO4 leaves no unexplained peaks.

{"present": ["mp-14005"], "confidence": 0.9, "note": "All main observed peaks (16.85, 25.25, 27.15, 31.5, 44.4, 50.3, 55.3 degrees) match simulated KRuO4 in position and intensity, and anatase is ruled out because its strong peak near 48 degrees is absent."}
